It reports descriptive shares (e.g., teacher age/gender composition, experience, perceived ability to adapt teaching to diversity, special education needs context, social and emotional learning support, and technology/AI use) and highlights only statistically significant differences or changes relative to an OECD average. The note does not conduct student-level predictive modeling, does not report model performance metrics, and does not describe plausible values or PV-based scaling because TALIS relies on self-reports rather than cognitive achievement PVs. It also cautions that cross-country comparisons should be interpreted carefully due to the self-report nature of the measures and potential social/cultural influences. Variance cautions are included for some estimates (e.g., higher risk of non-response bias), and the note directs readers to specific OECD TALIS 2024 database tables for the underlying computations.
